title: Model registry migrations for metadata schema v1 (storage + backfill + rollback)
creator: Ethan Park
project: Model metadata schema v1 + automated changelog generator
description:
Migrate existing model registry records to the Model Metadata Schema v1 storage layout. Implement a safe backfill and rollout plan across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, including sequencing, validation, monitoring, and rollback. This is the data-plane prerequisite for changelog generation + Console model history views.

Context / problem
- Today, model/version info is split across legacy registry fields (name/version/arch flags), runtime config, and docs/release notes.
- We’re standardizing on metadata schema v1 as the source-of-truth for model versioned information.
- We must migrate without breaking: pinned model versions, Private offline bundles, or the existing catalog APIs.

References
- Confluence schema: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/model-metadata-schema-v1.json
- ADR (source of truth / publishing): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0142-model-metadata-source-of-truth-and-publishing.json
- PR for migration work (expected landing): sources/github/redwood-model-registry/pr-18429-migrate-model-records-to-metadata-v1-backfill-and-rollback.json
- CI/pipeline checks: sources/confluence/eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build/schema-validation-and-release-note-build-pipeline.json

Goals
1) Add storage support for metadata_v1 for all model versions/variants/quantization profiles.
2) Backfill existing model records to metadata_v1 with clear provenance + risk classification.
3) Introduce dual-read/dual-write period with feature flags and verification.
4) Provide a rollback path that restores legacy reads/writes with minimal manual intervention.
5) Ensure public vs internal field separation remains intact during migration (redaction rules and access control are enforced; no internal-only notes leak into customer-visible views).

Non-goals
- Rewriting historical customer release notes beyond minimal backfill required for launch.
- Consolidating every legacy field into metadata_v1 on day 1 (we will preserve legacy columns during transition).

Proposed storage design (registry DB)
- Add new column (or new table) to store metadata_v1 payload as JSON (canonical schema), plus a schema hash/version for validation.
- Persist both:
  a) metadata_v1_public (customer-visible subset)
  b) metadata_v1_internal (full payload)
  Rationale: makes it easier to enforce redaction at read boundaries and avoid accidental overexposure in downstream services. Exact fields and filtering rules are defined in ENG-9825.

- Required supporting columns (indexed):
  - metadata_v1_schema_version (string, e.g., "1.0")
  - metadata_v1_schema_hash (string, for traceability; aligns with eval harness tagging)
  - metadata_v1_migrated_at (timestamp)
  - metadata_v1_migration_source (string enum: legacy_backfill | manual_edit | api_write)

- Backfill job writes metadata_v1_* without modifying legacy columns.

Migration sequencing / rollout plan
Phase 0 — Prep (dev + staging)
- Confirm schema validation tooling from ENG-9821 is available as a library usable by backfill.
- Inventory of existing models + gaps (see Drive inventory referenced in kickoff; used to estimate % that can be auto-backfilled vs needs manual patching).
- Decide default behaviors for missing fields (must be explicit and documented; do not silently invent compatibility claims).

Phase 1 — DB migration (add columns / table)
- Ship additive migration only; no destructive operations.
- Add read path (behind flag) to fetch metadata_v1 if present.
- Add metrics to compare legacy-derived view vs metadata_v1 view for key endpoints.

Phase 2 — Backfill (staging → prod canary)
- Implement idempotent backfill job:
  - Select model_version rows missing metadata_v1.
  - Generate metadata_v1 payload from legacy fields + known model family defaults.
  - Run schema validation; if invalid, mark row with migration error and skip publish.
  - Store payload + migration provenance.

- Canary in prod:
  - Run backfill for a small allowlist of low-risk models (e.g., internal/test + 1–2 public models with low usage).
  - Verify downstream consumers (Console feed, docs generator, SDK endpoints) can read without regressions.

Phase 3 — Dual-read verification
- Enable dual-read in control plane / model registry API (flagged):
  - Continue serving legacy API responses, but internally compute metadata_v1-derived response and compare for invariants.
  - Log diffs to a dedicated dashboard; alert on breaking diffs.

Phase 4 — Default to metadata_v1 for internal consumers
- Switch internal services (changelog generator ingestion, rollout policy engine eligibility checks) to use metadata_v1 first.
- Keep legacy as fallback for a fixed window (2–4 weeks).

Phase 5 — Default to metadata_v1 for customer-visible APIs (incremental)
- Enable for Hosted first, then Dedicated, then Private export tooling.
- Continue to support pinned legacy versions by mapping them to metadata_v1 records.

Phase 6 — Deprecate legacy fields (later)
- Only after stability window + documentation. Not in MVP.

Backfill strategy details
- Auto-backfill mapping rules:
  - semantic_version: derive from existing version strings where possible; if legacy uses non-semver, map to "0.0.0+legacy.<id>" and mark as legacy_mapped.
  - compatibility: only assert known runtime/tokenizer requirements (from registry + runtime config defaults). Otherwise set to "unknown" and require manual update before promotion.
  - availability: infer by existing deployment flags; do not assume Private availability.
  - deprecations: do not create new deprecations during backfill.
  - quality/safety notes: do not generate subjective claims; leave empty unless previously documented.

- Manual patch flow:
  - For records failing validation or missing mandatory fields, create a follow-up task list for Quentin Harris (schema owner) + model catalog ICs.
  - Backfill job outputs a CSV report (or table) of failures with reasons and suggested remediations.

Validation + safety checks
- Hard validation (job fails row): JSON Schema validation, required fields, public/internal separation constraints.
- Soft validation (job warns): unknown compatibility, missing eval tags, missing rollout eligibility.
- Pre-promotion guard (outside this ticket but we must support it): control plane promotion flow requires metadata_v1 present + validated.

Monitoring
- Metrics to add (tagged by deployment mode and model family):
  - migration_backfill_rows_total / success / failed
  - metadata_v1_read_rate (by endpoint)
  - legacy_vs_v1_diff_count (for computed invariants)
  - docs_build_release_notes_missing_metadata (should trend to 0)

- Dashboards: link to observability pack work correlating change events (see sources/github/observability-pack/pr-612-dashboard-panel-model-version-change-rate-and-rollout-correlation.json).

Failure modes and mitigations
1) Bad backfill produces incorrect compatibility constraints → could block legitimate traffic or mislead customers.
   - Mitigation: conservative defaults; do not assert constraints we don’t know. Keep legacy fallback until confidence is high.

2) Partial migration leads to missing release notes for a promotion.
   - Mitigation: promotion gate checks metadata presence; CI preview artifacts highlight missing required fields.

3) Internal-only fields leak into customer-visible API/Console.
   - Mitigation: store public/internal separately; enforce filtering at read boundaries; add regression tests aligned with ENG-9825.

4) Private upgrade bundle generation cannot resolve metadata_v1 offline.
   - Mitigation: ensure export tooling includes metadata_v1 payloads and schema hash; validate in offline build flow (ENG-9829 dependency for end-to-end).

Rollback plan
- Rollback trigger criteria:
  - Significant increase in 5xx/latency on model catalog endpoints correlated with metadata_v1 reads.
  - Evidence of customer-visible data corruption (wrong version shown, wrong availability).
  - Any internal-only field exposure incident.

- Rollback steps (no data loss):
  1) Flip feature flags to force legacy reads for all endpoints.
  2) Stop backfill job / disable scheduler.
  3) Keep metadata_v1 columns populated (do not delete) for forensic analysis.
  4) If a specific model record is malformed, mark metadata_v1_invalid and exclude from v1 reads.

- Forward-fix process:
  - Patch mapping rules or manual overrides.
  - Re-run backfill idempotently for affected rows.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] DB migration is additive and deployed safely to staging + prod.
- [ ] Backfill job is idempotent and can be resumed; produces failure report.
- [ ] >= 95% of currently served Hosted models have valid metadata_v1 payloads (public + internal).
- [ ] Dual-read diff dashboard is live; diff rate under agreed threshold for 7 consecutive days.
- [ ] Documented rollback playbook exists and has been exercised in staging.
- [ ] Security/compliance sign-off on public/internal separation strategy for stored fields.

Open questions
- Do we want metadata_v1_public physically stored, or compute at read time and cache? (Current proposal stores both to reduce leak risk and simplify downstream.)
- What’s the canonical mapping for legacy non-semver versions? (Need alignment with Quentin + Release Eng so it doesn’t confuse customers.)
- What is the minimum metadata_v1 completeness threshold to allow a model promotion in Hosted? (PM decision; we can implement a strict default with allowlist exceptions.)
